Order 
This appeal has been filed by the appellant/Insurance Company under Section 173 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 against the award dated 24.11.2018 passed by 4th AMACT, District Chhindwara in MACC No.168/2016, 169/2016 and 170/2016 seeking exoneration from liability to pay the compensation/reduction of compensation.

2 . Learned counsel for the appellant-Insurance Company after referring to Circular No.S.O.1248(E)
Dated 05.11.2004 issued by Central Government submits that in the instant case, offending vehicle is a dumper and as per above Circular, dumper comes within the definition of transport vehicle.

Therefore, for driving dumper on public road, permit and fitness are required but in the instant case, owner and driver have not filed any permit or NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:1055 2 MA-1148-2019 fitness certificate, therefore, offending vehicle was being driven in violation of terms and conditions of insurance policy.
3. Learned counsel for the appellant further submits that at the time of accident, deceased was riding the motorcycle with two children and his wife.
At the time of accident, deceased was not having any valid licence to ride the motorcycle.

Thus, at the time of accident, deceased was riding Oriental Insurance Company Limited vs Smt. Neetu on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191418482/
1 the motorcycle in breach of Sections 3 and 5 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

sentences.text: Further, after referring to depositions of applicant witness Neetu Pawar, it is urged that deceased has hit the dumper from behind.
Hence, deceased was riding the motorcycle negligently.
Thus, he has also contributed to the happening of the accident and at least 25% should have been deducted for contributory negligence on the part of the deceased in claim case no.168/2016.

Further, after referring to para-10 of the impugned award, it is urged that Tribunal has awarded Rs.1,40,000/- under the head of consortium whereas in view of law laid down in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi AIR 2017 SC 5157, that wife is entitled to receive Rs.40,000/- for consortium and not Rs.1,40,000/-.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi AIR 2017 SC 5157
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, it has been prayed that the appeal filed by the appellant/Insurance Company be allowed and Insurance Company be exonerated from liability to pay compensation/compensation be reduced.

4 . Learned counsel for the respondents/ owner and driver, after referring to para-8 of the impugned award submits that appellant/Insurance Company, did not obtain any information from RTO and had also not conducted any enquiry as to the requirement of permit/fitness certificate of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:1055 3 MA-1148-2019 the vehicle.

It is also urged that burden to prove breach of terms and conditions of insurance policy is on the Insurance Company but in the instant case, Insurance Company did not adduce any evidence to prove that at the time of accident,
offending vehicle was being driven in violation of terms and conditions of insurance policy.

Therefore, in the instant case, it is not established that at the time of accident, offending vehicle was driven in violation of terms and conditions of insurance policy, Therefore, appeal filed by the appellant-Insurance Company be dismissed.
5.

Learned counsel for the respondents 1 -3/claimants submits that from para 4 of testimony of applicant witness Chansawali Dhurve, it is evident that immediately prior to the accident, offending vehicle was parked by the side of the road and all of a sudden, driver of offending vehicle, started the vehicle and took it on the road and on account of which, motorcycle got collided with offending vehicle.
Further, insurance company did not take defence pertaining to absence of driving licence.
Therefore, it cannot be said that deceased contributed in any manner whatsoever to the happening of the accident.
Therefore, no amount could be deducted for contributory negligence on the part of the deceased.
On above grounds, it has been prayed that the appeal filed by the appellant/insurance company be dismissed.

6. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.
ANALYSIS AND FINDINGS:-
7. First issue involved in the case is whether for driving offending NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:1055 4 MA-1148-2019 vehicle on public road i.e. Caterpillar 424B Bachloe Loader,
any permit/fitness is required ?
8. Admittedly, in the instant case, accident occurred from Caterpillar 424B Bachloe Loader.

Perusal of insurance policy Ex.D/1 reveals that therein, under the head, " Limitations as to use " it is mentioned that " The policy covers use only under a permit within the meaning of the Motor Vehicle Oriental Insurance Company Limited vs Smt. Neetu on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191418482/
2 Act, 1988 ..................."

entities.text: Motor Vehicle Oriental Insurance Company Limited vs Smt. Neetu
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, in Circular No.S.O.1248(E) Dated 05.11.2004 issued by Central Government, it is mentioned that however, when the public road is being used regularly for carrying on commercial activities, then, construction equipment vehicles such as Dumpers and Excavators being used for such activities shall be deemed as transport vehicles.
As per Motor Vehicles Act/Rules framed thereunder, a transport vehicle cannot be used on public road without a valid permit/fitness.

9. In view of above, especially, insurance policy Ex.D/1, appellant/insurance company was not required to enquire with RTO or make any other enquiry as to the requirement of permit/fitness with respect to offending vehicle.
In the instant case, owner and driver of offending vehicle has been present before the Tribunal and they are present in appeal also before this Court but till today, no permit/fitness etc.
has been filed in the instant case.
Therefore, it will be presumed that on the date of accident, offending vehicle was being driven without any permit/fitness etc..
It is correct that generally, insurance company is required to prove that vehicle was being driven in breach of terms and conditions of insurance policy.

But as in the instant case, owner and driver of offending vehicle are present and NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:1055 5 MA-1148-2019 they have not filed any permit or fitness, therefore, insurance company was not obliged to lead any evidence with respect to absence of permit/fitness on the date of accident.
10. Hence, in this Court's considered opinion, learned Tribunal has wrongly held that appellant failed to prove that permit/fitness was required to operate/ply offending vehicle on public road.

Thus, in the instant case, from evidence on record, it is clearly established that at alleged date, time and place, offending vehicle was being driven in violation of terms and conditions of insurance policy i.e. without any valid permit or fitness.
11. Next issue before this Court is whether deceased contributed in any manner whatsoever to the happening of the accident.
12. It is correct that in the instant case, at the time of accident, deceased was riding the motorcycle with two children (aged 2 years and 5 years) along with his wife on the motorcycle.

Further, in view of para 13 of applicant witness Neetu, wife of deceased, it is evident that at the time of accident,
deceased was not having any licence to drive the motorcycle.

But it is well established that just on the basis of absence of driving licence or that more than two persons were sitting on the motorcycle,
it cannot be said that the person riding the motorcycle was riding it rashly and negligently, without there being any other evidence on record.
13. Now question arises as to whether there is any other evidence on record to show that at the time of accident, deceased was riding the motorcycle rashly and negligently.

14. Applicant witness Neetu Pawar has admitted in her cross- NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:1055 6 MA-1148-2019 examination that their motorcycle was hit by back portion of the machine and accident occurred on account of the same.
Applicant witness Chansawali Dhurve has deposed in his cross-examination that on 16.04.2016 at about 07:00 in the evening, he was returning to his house from the field.

A motorcycle was going in Oriental Insurance Company Limited vs Smt. Neetu on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191418482/
3 front of him.

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Company Limited vs Smt. Neetu
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: At that time, on the main road, driver of loader machine Arcon Company, suddenly moved/turned it on the middle of the road, on account of which, back portion of loader machine hit the motorcycle, which was going in front of him.

This witness has further stated in his cross-examination that loader was parked and all of a sudden, driver started it and brought it on the middle of the road and turned it, on account of which, it hit the motorcycle on the middle road.
15. Further, in the instant case, after investigation, charge sheet had been filed against the driver of the offending vehicle for driving the vehicle rashly and negligently.

It is also evident from record of the case that driver of offending vehicle did not lodge any report against rider of motorcycle to the effect that he was riding motorcycle rashly and negligently and on account of rash and negligent driving on the part of deceased, accident occurred.

Again in the instant case, driver and owner of offending vehicle have remained present before the Tribunal and they have also filed written statement and cross-examined applicant witnesses but they did not examine driver of offending vehicle whereas he was the best witness on the point that if accident did not occur on account of his negligence, then, how did it occur.
No explanation has been furnished for not examining the driver of the offending vehicle.
Hence, adverse inference is to be drawn against him.

It is NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:1055 7 MA-1148-2019 also evident from the record of the case that the appellant/Insurance Company also did not call driver of offending vehicle in the witness box and examined him on the point as to how and why accident occurred and who was responsible for the happening of the accident.
16. Hence, in view of discussion in the forgoing paras, it cannot be said that deceased also contributed to the happening of the accident in any manner whatsoever.
Therefore, no amount can be deducted under the head of contributory negligence on the part of the deceased.
17. Learned counsel for the appellant/Insurance Company has also submitted that Tribunal has awarded excess amount under the head of consortium.
18. Perusal of impugned award reveals that learned Tribunal in Claim Case No.168/2016 in para 10 has awarded Rs.1,40,000/- for loss of consortium to wife of deceased.
In view of law laid down in the case of Pranay Sethi (supra), wife of deceased is entitled to receive only Rs.40,000/- under the head of consortium and not Rs.1,40,000/-.

Hence, Tribunal has erred in awarding Rs.1,40,000/-
under the head of consortium.
19. Hence, in view of discussion in the forgoing paras, compensation awarded by the Tribunal in paras 11 and 12 of the impugned award, is reduced to Rs.15,69,000/-.

20. So far as liability to pay the compensation is concerned, from discussion in the foregoing paras,
it is clearly established that at the time of accident, offending vehicle was being driven in violation of terms and conditions of insurance policy without any valid permit and fitness.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:1055 8 MA-1148-2019
Therefore, insurance company is exonerated from liability to pay the compensation.
But in the instant case, claimant is a third party, therefore, it would be appropriate to apply principle of pay and recover.

sentences.text: Hence, in view of above, in this Court's considered opinion, learned Tribunal has erred in not exonerating insurance company from liability to pay the compensation and not applying the principle of pay and recover.
22. Therefore, in view of facts discussed in the preceding paras, it would be just and appropriate to apply the principle of 'pay and recover'.

Hence, it is directed that the appellant-Insurance Company shall deposit the entire compensation amount (Rs.15,96,000/-) along with interest but thereafter, it will be at liberty to recover the same from the owner and driver of the offending vehicle provided in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Swaran Singh & Others-2004 ACJ 1 (SC); Amrit Paul Sing Vs.
TATAAIG General Insurance Co. Ltd.-AIR 2018 SC 2662; Shammana Vs. Divisional Manager Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd-AIR 2018 SC 3726/Sec.174 Motor Vehicles Act.
23.

24. Accordingly, appeal filed by the appellant/Insurance Company is partly allowed to the extent as indicated herein above and the same is disposed of.
